palace_guide.text: Welcome to the Bishop's Palace, built in the 12th century, almost as old as the cathedral next door.
In 1263 King Haakon IV of Norway came this way after the Battle of Largs. He fell ill and died here.
Orkney stayed Norse until 1468, when it was pledged to Scotland as part of the dowry of Margaret of Denmark. Nobody ever paid to get it back.
Next door are the ruins of the Earl's Palace, built about 1600 by Earl Patrick Stewart. Quite a bit grander, quite a bit more roof missing.
